links.outcome: Diagnostic revisions leading to patient recall, with vs without AI fracture detection
links.effect: Diagnostic revisions 8.6% without AI vs 5.7% with AI (RR 0.66; 95% CI 0.37-1.19). Therapeutic changes 2.0% vs 0.4% (p = 0.10). No significant differences in secondary endpoints.
links.quote: Diagnostic revisions occurred in 8.6% without AI, in 5.7% with AI support (risk ratio 0.66; 95% CI 0.37-1.19).

links.outcome: Clinician performance and workflow outcomes with vs without AI assistance in the intended deployment mode
links.effect: Senior consultation 14.3% vs 12.5%, length of stay 2.3 h vs 2.4 h, and subjective diagnostic confidence showed no significant differences with AI.
links.quote: No significant differences were observed for secondary endpoints, including need for senior consultation (14.3% vs. 12.5%), subjective diagnostic confidence, or length of stay (2.3 h vs. 2.4 h).

screen.reason: Prospective clinical trial evaluating the impact of real-time AI fracture detection assistance for treating physicians in a pediatric emergency department on clinical outcomes like patient recalls and diagnostic revisions.
